"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 3456: a "difference vs. pairing" direction.

What it does, in plain terms
- Its output direction, read through the unembedding, promotes the words
  "difference", "differences", "distinction", "different" (and 区别 / 差异 / 不同).
  So it leans positive while the text is discussing how things differ or contrast.
- Its activation is negative where two things are being grouped together:
  "both", "two", "together", "either", "neither", "each other", "respectively".

This program is a short keyword rule: it looks at the last few tokens of the
same document and adds a small positive value if a contrast word appears, and a
small negative value if a pairing word appears. Everything else gets 0.

Honest scope: this captures only a small part of the activation. Most of its
variance sits in diffuse, large swings on ordinary tokens (periods, "the",
commas) that no word list describes, so the rule explains very little variance.
"""
import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

WINDOW = 10  # how many recent tokens of the same document to look at
CONTRAST = re.compile(r"differ|distinct|contrast|unlike|versus|区别|差别|差异|不同|отлич", re.I)
PAIRING = re.compile(r"^(both|two|together|either|neither|respectively)$|^each other$", re.I)
CONTRAST_VALUE = 0.26  # fitted on a 10k-row sample of training data
PAIRING_VALUE = -0.07


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    lo = max(0, t - WINDOW)
    recent = [
        s.strip().lower()
        for i, s in enumerate(prefix.token_strings[lo : t + 1], start=lo)
        if prefix.document_ids[i] == prefix.document_ids[t]
    ]
    contrast = any(CONTRAST.search(s) for s in recent)
    pairing = any(PAIRING.match(s) for s in recent)
    return carry, CONTRAST_VALUE * contrast + PAIRING_VALUE * pairing

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3457: a weak, diffuse, mostly-negative writer.

What the component reads: almost only MLP hidden unit 3457 of layer 15. Its activation
is about -0.03 on average with spread about 0.35 at nearly every token, and most of that
spread is not readable: token identity, previous token, token class and position each
explain under 6% of it.

What it does respond to (the one clear pattern): the descriptor in an encyclopedic
definition such as "X is an American politician", "Y was a former ...", "Z is a
Norwegian ...". The component goes strongly negative on the nationality (or "former",
"professional", "retired") right after "is/was/are/were a/an" (about -2.5), on the
word after that descriptor (about -1.6), and more weakly on other words after "is a/an"
(about -0.4) and on nationality words anywhere else (about -0.2). Everywhere else it
predicts the component's typical value, -0.03.

This program covers those cases only. It explains about 0.6% of the variance; the
remaining variance is not captured by any simple concept we found.

The program is stateless and causal: it reads the last few tokens of the same document.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

BASELINE = -0.03  # the component's mean activation
DESCRIPTOR = -2.5  # "is a/an <nationality or former>"
OTHER_SLOT = -0.4  # "is a/an <any other word>"
PHRASE = -1.6  # the word after "is a/an <nationality or former>"
NOUN_ELSEWHERE = -0.2  # a nationality or "former" in any other position

NATIONALITIES = {
    "American", "British", "English", "Scottish", "Welsh", "Irish", "French", "German",
    "Spanish", "Italian", "Portuguese", "Dutch", "Belgian", "Swiss", "Austrian", "Swedish",
    "Norwegian", "Danish", "Finnish", "Icelandic", "Polish", "Czech", "Slovak", "Hungarian",
    "Romanian", "Bulgarian", "Greek", "Russian", "Ukrainian", "Serbian", "Croatian",
    "Turkish", "Georgian", "Armenian", "Japanese", "Chinese", "Korean", "Indian",
    "Pakistani", "Bangladeshi", "Thai", "Vietnamese", "Filipino", "Indonesian", "Malaysian",
    "Australian", "Canadian", "Mexican", "Brazilian", "Argentine", "Argentinian", "Chilean",
    "Colombian", "Peruvian", "Venezuelan", "Cuban", "Jamaican", "Egyptian", "Israeli",
    "Iranian", "Iraqi", "Lebanese", "Nigerian", "Kenyan", "Ghanaian", "Ethiopian",
    "Moroccan", "Algerian", "Tunisian", "Zimbabwean", "Zambian", "Ugandan", "Taiwanese",
    "Singaporean", "Nepalese", "Mongolian", "Kazakh", "Uzbek", "Azerbaijani", "Albanian",
    "Latvian", "Lithuanian", "Estonian", "Slovenian", "Bosnian", "Macedonian", "Maltese",
}
DESCRIPTORS = NATIONALITIES | {"former", "professional", "retired"}

ARTICLES = {" a", " an"}
COPULAS = {" is", " was", " are", " were"}
PUNCTUATION = set(".,;:!?()[]{}\n\r\"'")


def _is_word(token: str) -> bool:
    return token.strip() != "" and not any(c in PUNCTUATION for c in token)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids

    def same_doc(back: int) -> bool:
        return t - back >= 0 and docs[t - back] == docs[t]

    def word(back: int) -> str:
        return toks[t - back].strip()

    value = BASELINE
    if not _is_word(toks[t]) or not same_doc(1):
        return carry, float(value)
    if word(0) in DESCRIPTORS:
        value = NOUN_ELSEWHERE
    if t >= 2 and same_doc(2) and toks[t - 1] in ARTICLES and toks[t - 2] in COPULAS:
        value = DESCRIPTOR if word(0) in DESCRIPTORS else OTHER_SLOT
    elif t >= 3 and same_doc(3) and toks[t - 2] in ARTICLES and toks[t - 3] in COPULAS:
        if _is_word(toks[t - 1]) and word(1) in DESCRIPTORS:
            value = PHRASE
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3458, read through its down_proj component.

What it does: this is a diffuse neuron. Its activation is mostly near zero, with rare
large positive spikes (up to about 27 on training rows) and smaller negative dips. Tested
against simple features, none explains much: token identity (held-out about 1%), token
class (about 0), the model's surprisal at the token (about 0), and the document's average
level (an oracle gets about 3%). The one weak signal found is repetition: the activation is
somewhat higher when the current token completes a two-token pair (previous token, current
token) that already appeared earlier in the same document. This program predicts the mean
activation in each case: about 0.093 if the pair repeats earlier text, about 0.048
otherwise. On eval it explains about 0.05% of the variance, so it is a weak description.

Why: a person reading it learns that this neuron carries little that is predictable from
simple features of the text. Its switched-off effect on the output is negligible.
"""

READS = ()

REPEATED_PAIR = 0.093
NEW_PAIR = 0.048


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        seen = set()
    else:
        seen = carry[1]
    tokens = prefix.token_ids
    repeated = False
    if len(tokens) >= 2 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == doc:
        pair = (tokens[-2], tokens[-1])
        repeated = pair in seen
        seen.add(pair)
    return (doc, seen), (REPEATED_PAIR if repeated else NEW_PAIR)

"""Explanation of p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3459.

What it is: one rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down-projection. It reads a
diffuse direction of the layer-15 MLP hidden state (its input vector spreads
its weight over thousands of hidden units; hidden unit 3459 itself is only
about a fifth of that vector's length) and writes along one fixed direction
of the residual stream.

What it responds to: nothing simple that I could find. Its activation has
mean about -0.035 and standard deviation 0.55 over training tokens, and:
- token class (digits, punctuation, words, whitespace) and position in the
  document barely shift it (position 1 to 3 averages +0.17, the rest about -0.03);
- whether the token occurred earlier in the document makes no real difference;
- a lookup of the average value per token identity, fitted on training rows,
  explains about 2 percent of held-out variance at best, and the tokens that
  move it most (code and shell words, hedging adverbs) do not form a clean concept.
Its values are only weakly correlated from one token to the next (lag-1 0.3).

So this program predicts the component's typical value at every position.
Switching the component off already moves the model's next-token distribution
by only about 5e-6 nats per position, so the constant changes nothing measurable.
"""

READS = ()

# The component's mean activation over training tokens.
MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.035


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 3460 (the component's activation is this unit's value, times ~1).

What it is: the component reads one hidden unit of layer 15's MLP and writes it back
along a direction that, read through the unembedding, favours words such as "predictable",
"trivial", "obvious", "mundane", "commonplace", "easy" and "old".

What it responds to (from reading its top and bottom windows): it is positive in casual
prose that calls something obvious, trivial, easy, old, already said or not novel ("nothing
new under the sun", "the ground has been often trod", "easily guessable", "quickly solved",
"not all that challenging"). It is negative in formal mathematical working: equations,
digits, "hence", "therefore", proofs and derivations.

Honest limit: the unit is diffuse. Its values are mostly small and vary from one token to
the next with context, and no token list explains more than about 0.1% of its variance.
This program keeps the concept, not a fit: a decaying tally of triviality words and of
maths-looking tokens within the current document, and a prediction of their weighted sum.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that call something obvious, trivial, easy, old, familiar or not novel.
TRIVIAL = frozenset(
    """obvious obviously trivial simple simply easy easily quick quickly boring mundane
    ordinary common commonplace generic familiar known old often already again redundant
    predictable useless pointless novelty unremarkable remarkable guessable solved""".split()
)
# Characters that mark formal mathematics or code-like working.
MATH_MARKS = frozenset("=²³⇒∑∫√≤≥<>^\\$*/+")

DECAY = 0.5  # how fast the tallies forget earlier tokens
W_TRIVIAL = 0.18  # activation per unit of triviality tally
W_MATH = -0.013  # activation per unit of maths tally
BIAS = -0.018  # the unit's typical value (its mean is about -0.02)


def is_math(text: str) -> bool:
    return any(ch.isdigit() or ch in MATH_MARKS for ch in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    trivial, maths = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, 0.0)
    # A new document starts fresh: forget the tallies at a document boundary.
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) >= 2 and ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        trivial, maths = 0.0, 0.0
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip().lower().strip(".,!?;:\"'“”’")
    trivial = DECAY * trivial + (1.0 if word in TRIVIAL else 0.0)
    maths = DECAY * maths + (1.0 if is_math(text) else 0.0)
    value = BIAS + W_TRIVIAL * trivial + W_MATH * maths
    return (trivial, maths), value

"""Predict the component's activation from whether the current token is made of letters.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3461 is a rank-one piece of layer 15's
MLP output. Its activation is diffuse: it is not tied to particular tokens, and token
classes explain under 1% of its variance. The one split that holds is letters versus the
rest: tokens containing a letter (words, names, CJK characters) sit a bit below zero, while
punctuation, digits, spaces and newlines sit near zero. This program predicts those two
average values.
"""

import regex

READS = ()

LETTER_MEAN = -0.083
OTHER_MEAN = -0.017


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if regex.search(r"\p{L}", text):
        return None, LETTER_MEAN
    return None, OTHER_MEAN

"""Sentence and line boundaries, as a negative push.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3462 mostly goes negative when the
text closes a sentence or a line. It is near zero on ordinary words and commas, and
slightly positive in some code and chat markup, which this program ignores.

This program predicts a fixed value for each class of token:
  - a sentence-final mark (. ! ? 。) alone:             about -1.0
  - the same mark with a line break in the token (.\n): about -1.9
  - a closing bracket ) or ] ending a clause:           about -0.4
  - a line break (newline-only token):                   about -0.8
  - anything else:                                      0

The values are the class means on 8192 training rows. The sentence-to-sentence spread
(std about 2) is not captured.
"""
import re

READS = ()

SENTENCE_MARK = re.compile(r"[.!?。！？]\s*$")
CLOSING = re.compile(r"[)\]]\s*$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if SENTENCE_MARK.search(text):
        value = -1.9 if "\n" in text else -1.0
    elif CLOSING.search(text) and "\n" not in text:
        value = -0.4
    elif text.strip() == "" and "\n" in text:
        value = -0.8
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Acting-word detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3463.

The component goes negative on acting and film vocabulary. On the acting words themselves
it is strongly negative: "starring", "actor(s)", "actress", and Chinese "主演", "饰演",
"演技", "出演", "演员". In film and TV talk (cast lists, filmographies) it is mildly
negative, fading over the next tokens. Its negative direction promotes actor and acting
words as the next token. Most of its variance, the large negative spikes in cast lists
and other text, is not explained here.

The program reads only the prefix: a token's own value, plus a decaying count of film
words earlier in the same document.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

# Typical activation on the acting word itself.
ACTING = {
    "starring": -20.0,
    "starred": -11.0,
    "actor": -6.0,
    "actors": -8.0,
    "actress": -8.0,
    "actresses": -6.0,
    "acting": -1.0,
    "主演": -11.0,
    "饰演": -20.0,
    "演技": -7.0,
    "出演": -6.0,
    "演员": -7.0,
    "扮演": -5.0,
}

# Film and TV vocabulary that raises the film-context count.
FILM = {
    "film", "films", "movie", "movies", "cinema", "actor", "actors", "actress",
    "actresses", "acting", "cast", "role", "roles", "starring", "starred", "star",
    "stars", "performance", "director", "series", "episode", "episodes", "television",
    "tv", "drama", "sitcom", "portrayed", "played", "sequel",
}
FILM_ZH = ("电影", "导演", "角色", "影片")

DECAY = 0.95  # how fast the film-context count fades per token
SCALE = 0.5  # activation per unit of film-context count
CAP = 2.0  # largest count that counts


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    score = 0.0
    if carry is not None and len(doc) > 1 and doc[-1] == doc[-2]:
        score = carry
    if word in ACTING:
        value = ACTING[word]
    else:
        value = -SCALE * min(score, CAP)
    is_film = word in FILM or any(z in word for z in FILM_ZH)
    return score * DECAY + float(is_film), value

"""Layer 15, MLP down projection, component 3464: a near-constant predictor.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of the MLP's down projection. Its read
vector is almost entirely MLP hidden unit 15.3464 (weight 0.69 of a norm of 0.95;
every other unit carries at most 0.07), so its activation is roughly the scaled
value of that one hidden unit, with the rest spread thinly over the other units.

What it does in the model: switched off, it barely changes the output (KL about
3e-6 nats per position). Its activation is dense (std about 0.44, mostly within
+/-1) with rare spikes, mostly negative, up to about -12 at high causal importance.

What this program does: it predicts the component's mean value, -0.03, at every
position. None of the simple features tried predicted the activation out of
sample (token identity, token class, previous token, position in document,
whether the token or its continuation repeats earlier text, and repeat length):
their variance explained was at most about 0.3%. So this program explains
nothing beyond the mean, and it reproduces the switched-off component's effect.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Coarse predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3466.

This component has no clean trigger. Its activation is a dense, diffuse readout of
the layer-15 MLP hidden state: no single token, hidden unit or position explains much
of it. Token identity explains about 5% held out; a linear readout of all 2048 dims of
the normalized residual the MLP reads explains about 40%, but spread over every
dimension with no concept behind it. Its causal importance almost never passes
threshold, so switching it off barely changes the model's output.

What survives is coarse. Over training text it runs higher on line breaks, digits and
punctuation than on words, and it drifts downward as the token sits deeper into its
document. This program predicts that: a fixed offset by kind of token, plus a drift
with the log of the token's position in its document, restarting at each new document.
It explains about 3% of the variance. Predicting the mean alone explains none, and the
offsets are what add the 3%; a richer kind-by-word-frequency table reaches about 4%.
"""

import math

# Mean offset by kind of token, fit by least squares on training text.
KIND_OFFSET = {
    "newline": 0.33,
    "digit": 0.17,
    "punct": 0.18,
    "space": 0.15,
    "word": 0.15,
    "spaced_word": 0.09,
}
DRIFT = -0.05  # per unit of log(1 + position in document)

READS = ()


def kind(text):
    """The kind of one token, from its decoded text."""
    s = text.strip()
    if "\n" in text:
        return "newline"
    if not s:
        return "space"
    if s.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if all(not c.isalnum() for c in s):
        return "punct"
    if text.startswith(" "):
        return "spaced_word"
    return "word"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation predicted at position t: category offset plus drift with depth in document."""
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    depth = 0 if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry + 1
    value = KIND_OFFSET[kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])] + DRIFT * math.log1p(depth)
    return depth, value

"""Deliberation detector for layer 15 MLP down_proj component 3467.

The component writes a "second-guessing" signal into the residual stream. It is strongest
on the words that open a reconsideration in a model's chain of thought ("Alternatively",
"Wait", "Hmm", "perhaps", "maybe", "actually"), and on the self-talk words that come with
weighing approaches ("let me", "not sure", "might", "think", "better", "easier", "approach").
Those self-talk words are near zero in ordinary prose; they fire when the text is already
deliberating. So:

- the program keeps a deliberation level h: a count of the opener words in the same
  document, decaying by 0.85 per token, reset at each document boundary;
- each listed word gets a base activation plus a gain times h (the self-talk words are
  near zero until deliberation has started);
- every token gets a small share of h, because the whole stretch of reasoning sits a
  little above zero while the model is deliberating.
"""

READS = ()

# word: (base activation, gain per unit of deliberation level h)
TABLE = {
    "alternatively": (8.9, 0.8),
    "wait": (4.9, 0.0),
    "hmm": (5.0, 0.0),
    "perhaps": (3.9, 2.2),
    "maybe": (3.4, 2.0),
    "actually": (1.1, 2.7),
    "but": (0.7, 1.2),
    "me": (0.6, 4.9),
    "think": (0.8, 4.7),
    "approach": (0.9, 5.5),
    "better": (0.9, 8.0),
    "simpler": (3.9, 4.5),
    "easier": (2.9, 19.0),
    "might": (0.8, 6.9),
    "sure": (0.8, 11.5),
}
OPENERS = {"alternatively", "wait", "hmm", "perhaps", "maybe", "actually"}
DECAY = 0.85  # per token: the opener count fades over about 6 tokens
BACKGROUND = 1.0  # share of h that every token gets


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    h, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        h = 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    base, gain = TABLE.get(word, (0.0, 0.0))
    value = base + (gain + BACKGROUND) * h
    h = h * DECAY + (word in OPENERS)
    return (h, prefix.document_ids[-1]), value

"""Year-digit detector: a weak, sparse read of the layer-15 MLP unit 3470's output.

The component (p-82af68dd, layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3470) reads a direction of the
layer-15 MLP hidden state and writes a small amount into the residual stream. Its
activation sits near -0.04 almost everywhere, with a noisy spread (std 0.32) that no
token identity, bigram or short token window predicts. Two readable features stand
out, and this program predicts those:

1. The LAST DIGIT OF A FOUR-DIGIT YEAR. When a number written with digits reaches
   its fourth digit and starts with 1 or 2, the activation rises. For years 1800-2029
   (numbers starting 18, 19 or 20) it is about +0.4 on average. Other 1xxx and 2xxx
   numbers stay near zero. Digits 1-3 of a number do not fire, and neither do digits
   of numbers longer than four digits (the program only sees the prefix, so it counts
   the digits in the run that ends at this token).
2. The SECOND TOKEN OF A DOCUMENT is pushed down, to about -0.28 on average. The
   first token of a document is near zero.

Everything else gets the baseline, the activation's typical value (-0.04).

Honest scope: together these explain under 1% of the activation's variance (about
0.7% on a sample of training rows). Most of the activation is a diffuse mixture
over many MLP units, with no concept behind it that we could find.
"""

READS = ()
BASELINE = -0.04  # the activation's typical value away from the features
MODERN_YEAR = 0.43  # fourth digit of 1800-2029
OTHER_NUMBER = 0.0  # fourth digit of another 1xxx or 2xxx number
SECOND_TOKEN = -0.28  # second token of a document
FIRST_TOKEN = 0.0  # first token of a document
DIGITS = "0123456789"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token. `carry` is (document id, position in document)."""
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    # Position within the document; positions restart where the document changes.
    if carry is None or docs[t] != carry[0]:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    carry = (docs[t], pos)
    if pos == 0:
        return carry, FIRST_TOKEN
    if pos == 1:
        return carry, SECOND_TOKEN
    # The run of digit tokens that ends at this token, within the same document.
    run = []
    i = t
    while i >= 0 and strings[i] in DIGITS and docs[i] == docs[t]:
        run.append(strings[i])
        i -= 1
    if len(run) != 4:
        return carry, BASELINE  # not a fourth digit, or the number is longer
    run.reverse()  # the number's digits, first to last
    if run[0] not in ("1", "2"):
        return carry, BASELINE
    if run[0] + run[1] in ("18", "19", "20"):
        return carry, MODERN_YEAR
    return carry, OTHER_NUMBER

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3472.

What it does (plain terms): this component is mostly quiet noise, but its strongest
responses are on markdown section headings. It goes clearly negative on the `#` marker
that opens a heading line (a `#`, `##`, `###`, ... token right after a line break,
as in "...\\n\\n### Introduction"), and is near zero everywhere else.

This program predicts that: -0.6 on a heading marker that starts a line in its
document, 0 at every other position. The value is the mean activation over such
heading markers in the training sample. It does not capture the large spread
within headings (from about -14 to +8), which depends on context this program cannot
see, nor the bulk of small activations, which no simple token rule explains.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

HEADING_MARKERS = {"#", "##", "###", "####", "#####"}
HEADING_VALUE = -0.6


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    marker = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip() in HEADING_MARKERS
    starts_line = "\n" in prefix.token_strings[-2]
    return carry, HEADING_VALUE if marker and starts_line else 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3473: a near-silent, context-driven signal.

What the component is: one rank-one piece of the MLP's output. Its activation is the
MLP hidden vector projected on one direction (times that direction's size). Most of the
time it is small (spread about 0.4, mean about -0.05), with rare excursions of several units
in either sign.

What we found: none of the simple readings predicts it. The current token, the previous
token, the token's script or word class, the position in a line, or whether the bigram
repeated earlier all leave its value almost unchanged. A linear fit on bag-of-context
features reaches only about 2% of its variance. So this program predicts the average
value everywhere, except that the first token of each document is 0, where the component is
always about zero.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids

"""Approximate-quantity detector: component 3474 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj.

In plain terms: the component fires when the text is in the middle of stating a rough amount,
such as "almost a year", "nearly 20 games", "roughly $10", "more than 300" or "about 2 km".
It does two things.

1. On the hedging word itself: strongly on "almost", "nearly", "roughly", "approximately" and
   their translations (casi, etwa, почти, 几乎, ほぼ ...), and more weakly on words that
   introduce an amount loosely: "over", "than" (as in "more/less than"), "about", "around",
   "few", "half", "several" and similar.
2. On the amount that follows a hedge: the number, the space before it, or a number word
   ("a", "two", "half") that comes within a few tokens after the hedge. This fades with
   distance, so the first token after "almost" carries most of the signal.

Everything else, including ordinary numbers with no hedge before them, is predicted as 0.
The rule explains about a sixth of the variance of the component's activation; the rest is
mostly spread over many small contexts and the component's exact magnitude.
"""

READS = ()

# Hedges that make the following amount approximate: strong (about 20 on the word),
# e.g. "almost", "nearly", "roughly", "approximately", and Chinese "超过" (more than) / "不到" (less than).
NEAR = set(
    "almost nearly roughly approximately virtually practically barely scarcely hardly quasi "
    "casi etwa circa почти практически 几乎 接近 大约 差不多 超过 不到 ほぼ ほとんど kaum".split()
)
# Words that introduce a loose amount: weaker (about 3 on the word, about 9 after).
BOUND = set(
    "over than about around few half several near approx under unos несколько mehr ~ 近 約".split()
)
# Words and marks that can carry the amount itself.
AMOUNT_WORDS = set(
    "a an one two three four five six seven eight nine ten twenty thirty fifty hundred "
    "thousand million billion dozen half few several couple".split()
)

NEAR_VALUE = 20.0      # on a strong hedge
NEAR_DECAY = 0.75      # per token after a strong hedge, on amount tokens
BOUND_VALUE = 3.2      # on a weak hedge
BOUND_AFTER = 9.0      # first amount token after a weak hedge
BOUND_DECAY = 0.8      # per further token
WINDOW = 6             # tokens after a hedge where its amount is still read


def is_amount(word):
    """A token that can be the amount: a digit, a number word, or the blank before digits."""
    return word == "" or word.isdigit() or word in AMOUNT_WORDS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        since_near = since_bound = 99  # no hedge yet in this document
    else:
        _, since_near, since_bound = carry
    since_near = 0 if word in NEAR else min(since_near + 1, 99)
    since_bound = 0 if word in BOUND else min(since_bound + 1, 99)

    amount = is_amount(word)
    value = 0.0
    if since_near == 0:
        value = NEAR_VALUE
    elif amount and since_near <= WINDOW:
        value = NEAR_VALUE * NEAR_DECAY**since_near
    if since_bound == 0:
        value = max(value, BOUND_VALUE)
    elif amount and since_bound <= WINDOW:
        value = max(value, BOUND_AFTER * BOUND_DECAY ** (since_bound - 1))
    return (doc, since_near, since_bound), value

The component is one SwiGLU hidden unit of layer 15, so its activation is
silu(gate) * up, scaled. Almost always it sits near zero. On rare tokens its
gate opens, and then the sign follows the kind of text:

  `next`, `temp`, `cur`, `head`, `->`);

CODE = re.compile(r"[;{}]|->|\t|==|#include|\bint\b|\bchar\b|\bvoid\b|\breturn\b")
# Loop and pointer words that the neuron responds to inside code.

# A capitalised word, as in a person's or award's name.

NAME_VALUE = -0.1  # mean activation on name words in prose

    code_count, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0, None)

MEAN = {
    ("syntax", "code"): -0.24,
    ("syntax", "prose"): -0.12,
    ("word", "code"): -0.18,
    ("word", "prose"): -0.025,
}


def token_kind(text: str) -> str:
    """'syntax' for whitespace, newlines and code symbols; 'word' otherwise."""
    if text.strip() == "" or "\n" in text or CODE_SYMBOLS.search(text):
        return "syntax"
    return "word"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids[t]
    # Recent tokens of the same document (the document resets attention and position).
    start = max(0, t - WINDOW)
    recent = [
        prefix.token_strings[i]
        for i in range(start, t)
        if prefix.document_ids[i] == doc
    ]
    symbol_share = (
        sum(1 for s in recent if CODE_SYMBOLS.search(s)) / len(recent) if recent else 0.0
    )
    context = "code" if symbol_share > CODE_SHARE else "prose"
    return carry, MEAN[(token_kind(prefix.token_strings[t]), context)]

This component is effectively unused. Its causal importance never passes the 0.1
threshold in the harvested corpus (0 of 10 million tokens), and switching it off
changes the model's next-token predictions by about 1e-6 nats per token. Its
activation is a diffuse, zero-mean signal (std about 0.3) with no clear concept
behind it: the identity of the current token explains only about 2% of its variance,
and no position rule explains more.

So this program predicts the average: exactly 0 at the first token of each document,
where the component is always about 0, and a small constant (the mean, about 0.005)
everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.005  # average over tokens after a document's first token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    first_in_document = len(ids) < 2 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first_in_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3508, read as a word-level guess.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of the MLP down projection. Its read direction loads
most heavily on the MLP's hidden unit 3508 (about 29% of its variance comes from that unit
alone; the rest is spread over thousands of units). Its output direction, read through the
unembedding, leans toward Chinese perfective 了 ("completed") and away from future or
conditional continuations (会, then, will). So, loosely, it leans toward "something finished"
versus "something still to come". This reading is suggestive, not established.

What this program does: it guesses the activation from the current word alone. Completion and
success words (completed, successfully, finished, passed, ready) get a positive value; every
other word gets the average value, a small negative number. That is the whole model.

It explains almost nothing. On held-out eval rows it explains about 0.05% of the variance, and
its switched-off effect on the output is negligible either way. A lookup table of every word's
average reaches only about 5% in-sample, so the activation depends mostly on context that no
single word shows; I found no simple context feature that does better.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words for finished or successful outcomes; the component's mean is highest on these.
DONE_WORDS = frozenset({"completed", "successfully", "finished", "passed", "ready"})

DONE_VALUE = 0.23  # mean activation on DONE_WORDS in the sample
REST_VALUE = -0.017  # mean activation on every other token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """The activation guess at the newest token: positive on completion words, else the mean."""
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, DONE_VALUE if word in DONE_WORDS else REST_VALUE

"""Math notation pushes this component negative.

The component is strongly negative on the symbols of algebra and arithmetic, and only weakly
so on ordinary text. Its largest response is to an operator (+ - = / ^ < > ...) that follows
an operand, a number or a single-letter variable, as in "x + y" or "2 - 3". Digits, single
letters and brackets are mildly negative, and more so next to symbols. Greek letter names and
LaTeX commands (\\tau, \\sqrt, \\cdot) and text inside $...$ count as math too. Ordinary prose,
spaces and most punctuation sit near zero.

The program reads only the newest token and the one before it, plus whether it is inside a
$...$ span, and returns the average activation for each pair of kinds. It explains about 10%
of the variance: the spread within each kind is mostly not captured.
"""

READS = ()

ARITH = set("+-−*/^=<>≤≥≠±×÷√∈")  # arithmetic, relation and root symbols
BRACKETS = set("()[]")
GREEK = set(
    "alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa lambda mu nu xi pi rho sigma "
    "tau upsilon phi chi psi omega".split()
)
MATH_WORDS = set(
    "times cdot sqrt partial infty ln exp cap cup sum int frac rightarrow leftarrow approx pm".split()
)

# Average activation by (kind of the newest token, kind of the token before it).
TABLE = {
    "op": {"letter": -4.1, "digit": -3.1, "symbol": -1.8, "text": -1.2},
    "digit": {"letter": -0.7, "digit": -0.3, "symbol": -1.9, "text": -0.9},
    "letter": {"letter": -0.8, "digit": -1.1, "symbol": -1.5, "text": -0.3},
    "latex": {"letter": -1.4, "digit": -1.4, "symbol": -1.3, "text": -0.8},
    "bracket": {"letter": -1.6, "digit": -1.0, "symbol": -0.8, "text": -0.6},
}
MATH_MODE_FACTOR = 1.5  # inside a $...$ span the values are scaled up


def kind(s):
    """The kind of one token's text, or None for ordinary text."""
    t = s.strip()
    if t and set(t) <= ARITH:
        return "op"
    if any(c in s for c in "\\{}_^$") or t.lstrip("\\").lower() in GREEK | MATH_WORDS:
        return "latex"
    if t.isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if len(t) == 1 and t.isalpha():
        return "letter"
    if t and set(t) <= BRACKETS:
        return "bracket"
    return None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # carry: whether we are inside a $...$ span (reset at each document start)
    inside = bool(carry) and same_doc
    if "$" in prefix.token_strings[-1]:
        inside = not inside
    k = kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    if k is None:
        return inside, 0.0
    before = "text"
    if same_doc:
        p = kind(prefix.token_strings[-2])
        before = {"op": "symbol", "bracket": "symbol", "latex": "symbol",
                  "letter": "letter", "digit": "digit"}.get(p, "text")
    factor = MATH_MODE_FACTOR if inside else 1.0
    return inside, TABLE[k][before] * factor

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3511, the simplest honest program.

What the component is: a rank-one slice of layer 15's MLP down-projection. Its activation
is a linear readout of the MLP's hidden state (mostly hidden unit 3511, plus a diffuse sum
of many small units), and that hidden state depends on the whole context in a way no
token list captures. Measured on ~4k training rows: token identity, the previous token,
a decayed bag of recent tokens, position, and clause distance together explain under 1%
of its variance. It is also nearly inert in the model (switching it off changes the
next-token distribution by ~1e-6 nats).

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value, about 0.04, at every
position, and 0 at the first token of each document, where the activation is ~0. It
captures the mean level and nothing else.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.04


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the mean activation, except 0 at the first token of a document."""
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or (
        prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3512 (the component's own neuron; its activation is that
unit's gated value, silu(gate) * up, times about 0.36).

What it does: almost nothing that a rule can read. Across ordinary tokens the value is
a zero-centred, noisy signal (std about 0.37). Its sign and size depend on context,
and no simple feature tracks it: token identity, token class (script, digit, punctuation,
subword), the previous token, position, and whether the token already occurred earlier
in the document each explain essentially none of its variance.

The one clear regularity is at the first token of each document, where this unit is
silent (value about 0). So the program predicts about 0 at each document's first token
and the average value (about -0.037) at every other token. A packed row can hold several
documents; a new document starts wherever the document label changes.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

DOCUMENT_START = -0.003
OTHER_TOKENS = -0.037


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, DOCUMENT_START if starts_document else OTHER_TOKENS

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3513 (its down_proj component), predicted coarsely.

What the unit does: it is a signed, context-driven feature. Almost none of its variance
comes from the current token alone (a per-token lookup explains nothing), and it is
nearly silent on the first token of each document. Its mean level depends only loosely on
the kind of token: it runs higher on digits, newlines, punctuation and other content
tokens, and sits near zero on English function words ("the", "of", "to", "is", ...). It
is also a little higher when the current token pair (previous token, current token) has
already appeared earlier in the same document, i.e. when text is repeating.

This program predicts those coarse levels. It explains only a small share of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    "a an the of to in on at by for with from as is are was were be been being it its this "
    "that these those and or but if so than then which who whom whose not no".split()
)

# Mean activation per token class (measured on training text).
LEVEL = {
    "function": 0.04,
    "digit": 0.29,
    "space": 0.22,
    "punct": 0.15,
    "non_ascii": 0.05,
    "spaced_word": 0.05,
    "other": 0.12,
}
REPEATED_PAIR_BONUS = 0.10


def token_class(text):
    word = text.strip().lower()
    if not text.strip():
        return "space"
    if text.startswith(" ") and word in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return "function"
    if any(c.isdigit() for c in text):
        return "digit"
    if not any(c.isalnum() for c in text):
        return "punct"
    if any(ord(c) > 127 for c in text):
        return "non_ascii"
    if text.startswith(" "):
        return "spaced_word"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        # A new document (or the row's first token): reset, and predict 0 there.
        seen = set()
        carry = (doc, seen, prefix.token_ids[-1])
        return carry, 0.0
    _, seen, prev = carry
    cur = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    pair = (prev, cur)
    value = LEVEL[token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])]
    if pair in seen:
        value += REPEATED_PAIR_BONUS
    seen.add(pair)
    return (doc, seen, cur), value

"""Predicts the activation of layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3514.

What the component is: a rank-one readout of layer 15's MLP hidden state. Its
activation is (hidden . v) * |u|, where v is dominated by hidden unit 3514 but has
many small weights on other units too. It is dense, with a roughly symmetric spread
of about +/-0.35, and it almost never passes the causal-importance threshold: it is
essentially switched off in the model, and zeroing it barely changes the output.

What the activation does track, weakly: its mean is near zero, and it is slightly
raised in the first few tokens of a document (positions 1 to 4 after a document
start), where it averages about +0.05 instead of about +0.01. Nothing about the
token identity, the token's character class or the previous token explains the
rest of its variance; those were checked and explain almost none of it.

So this program predicts that small document-start bump and a near-zero value
elsewhere. On the eval rows it explains about 0.01% of the variance (variance
explained 0.00013, Pearson r 0.013) and leaves the model's next-token predictions
essentially unchanged (kl_fraction 0.99, the same as switching the component off).
The rest of the activation is not captured by any concept I could find.
"""

READS = ()

EARLY_LO, EARLY_HI = 1, 4  # token indices inside a document that carry the small bump
EARLY_VALUE = 0.05  # mean activation there
BASE_VALUE = 0.01  # mean activation everywhere else


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or doc != carry[0]:
        index = 0  # first token of a new document
    else:
        index = carry[1] + 1
    if EARLY_LO <= index <= EARLY_HI:
        value = EARLY_VALUE
    else:
        value = BASE_VALUE
    return (doc, index), value

"""Travel and migration words: a weak, partial model of layer 15 MLP unit 3515.

The component is one MLP hidden unit of layer 15 (through down_proj), and its output
direction promotes travel words such as "journey", "trip" and "destination". It fires
inside clauses about going somewhere, moving or migrating. Its average is highest on the
travel or migration word itself (about 3 to 4), and the preposition that leads into a
destination after such a word averages about 1.5, with the largest single firings in
"deported *to*", "trip *to*", "sailed away *to* the", "traveled *to* England". It is near
zero or slightly negative elsewhere.

This program writes that down as three word tiers and a destination rule:
  - a travel or migration word gives 4, a movement verb or noun gives 1.5, and a common
    motion verb (go, came, return) gives 0.5;
  - a destination preposition (to, from, for, into, toward) within six tokens after a
    motion word gives 1.5.
Everything else gives 0. The levels are the average activations of those words in
training text. The program explains only the large positive firings: a word list cannot
capture most of the component's variance, which comes from context no word list describes.
"""

READS = ()

# Trip, voyage and migration words: the strongest firings (mean activation about 3 to 4).
TRAVEL = set(
    """sailed migrated deported abroad expedition voyage travel travels travelling
    traveling traveled trip trips journey journeys flew relocated overseas arrived
    settled""".split()
)

# Movement verbs and nouns: medium firing (about 1 to 1.5).
MOVEMENT = set(
    """moved sent returned ship tour headed ride gone visiting visit escape arrive left
    leave""".split()
)

# Common motion words: weak firing (about 0.3 to 0.5).
WEAK = set("go going goes came come went return move moving fly".split())

# Prepositions that introduce a destination.
DESTINATION = {"to", "from", "towards", "toward", "into", "for"}

WINDOW = 6  # tokens after a motion word in which a destination preposition still counts


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: the index of the last motion word in this document, or None."""
    words = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings]
    n = len(words)
    last = carry if carry is not None else -99
    if n == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        last = -99  # a new document starts: forget earlier motion words
    word = words[-1]
    if word in TRAVEL:
        level = 4.0
    elif word in MOVEMENT:
        level = 1.5
    elif word in WEAK:
        level = 0.5
    else:
        level = 0.0
    if level > 0:
        return n - 1, level
    if word in DESTINATION and 0 < n - 1 - last <= WINDOW:
        return last, 1.5
    return last, 0.0

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3516 of Qwen3-1.7B (component down_proj:3516).

The component reads this one hidden unit of the layer-15 MLP (its V vector is almost
entirely that unit), so its activation is that unit's value times the output norm.

What it responds to, in words a reader knows:
- words naming a kind or property in mathematics and logic ("integer", "odd",
  "positive", "rational", "linear", "convex", "finite", "valid", "invalid");
- words for a person's status or kind ("male", "amateur", "member", "player");
- hyphenated compound modifiers ("-digit", "-based", "-free", "-owned");
- adjective-forming suffix tokens ("-able", "-ic", "-ous", "-ive");
- ordinary property adjectives of technical text ("true", "false", "empty", "hidden").
It fires about twice as hard when such a word follows "is", "are", "be", "not",
"a" or "an", i.e. when it is predicated or introduced as a noun's modifier.
Almost every other token is near zero, and code/shell tokens are mildly negative.

This program is a readable lexicon: a listed token gets its fixed value, doubled after
a predicate or article word, and every other token gets 0. It explains only a small
share of the variance: the activation is spread over many tokens and contexts that
a short list cannot capture. A full per-token table would explain roughly four times
as much, but it would be a table of arbitrary token ids.
"""

READS = ()

# Mathematical and logical words used as adjectives or kinds of number or object.
MATH_WORDS = {
    "integer", "integers", "odd", "even", "positive", "negative", "real", "rational",
    "irrational", "prime", "composite", "palindrome", "numeric", "numerical", "quadratic",
    "cubic", "linear", "nonlinear", "convex", "finite", "infinite", "discrete",
    "continuous", "valid", "invalid", "binary", "symmetric", "homogeneous", "triangular",
    "rectangular", "circular", "horizontal", "vertical", "affine", "random", "empty",
    "optional", "async", "boolean",
}
# Words for a person's status or kind.
PERSON_WORDS = {
    "male", "female", "adult", "amateur", "professional", "member", "members", "player",
    "players", "participant", "living", "births", "human", "men", "fictional", "felony",
}
# Hyphenated compound modifiers, as the token they usually form.
COMPOUND_TOKENS = {
    "-digit", "-based", "-free", "-dimensional", "-like", "-owned", "-handed", "-profit",
    "-white", "-negative", "-linear", "-century",
}
# Suffix tokens that end adjectives.
ADJ_SUFFIXES = {"able", "ible", "ous", "ive", "ic", "ated", "ized", "ative", "ian"}
# Ordinary property adjectives, and privative "non" and "less", in technical text.
PROPERTY_WORDS = {
    "true", "false", "closed", "normal", "regular", "hidden", "private", "custom",
    "free", "small", "temporary", "digital", "fake", "independent", "non", "less",
}
# Words after which a word is being predicated or introduced as a modifier.
PREDICATE_WORDS = {" is", " are", " be", " was", " were", " not", " a", " an"}

WEIGHTS = (
    (MATH_WORDS, 1.7),
    (PERSON_WORDS, 1.3),
    (COMPOUND_TOKENS, 2.5),
    (ADJ_SUFFIXES, 1.0),
    (PROPERTY_WORDS, 1.0),
)


def _lexical_value(token: str) -> float:
    """The value a token's own text gives, before any context."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    for words, value in WEIGHTS:
        if word in words or token.lower() in words:
            return value
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """This component's activation at the newest token."""
    value = _lexical_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    if value == 0.0 or prefix.position == 0:
        return carry, 0.0
    same_document = prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_document else ""
    if previous in PREDICATE_WORDS:
        value *= 2.0
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 3518, read through its down_proj component 3518.

What this component is: one rank-one slice of the MLP's down projection. It reads the
MLP hidden vector and writes a small vector into the residual stream. Its input direction
puts 0.42 on hidden unit 3518 of layer 15 (about a quarter of its squared norm), so its
activation tracks that unit (correlation 0.54), with the rest spread over many units. Its
output norm is about 0.78. The component is nearly inert: switching it off changes the
next-token distribution by about 1e-6 nats per position.

What the search found: the activation is not predictable from the current token's identity,
its script or character class, or the previous token. Those explain about 0 of the variance
on held-out training positions. The one stable pattern is position in the document: the
activation leans slightly positive over the first few tokens and drifts slightly negative
deeper in. This program predicts that drift from the token's position within its document,
counted from the document's first token; the position resets at each document boundary.

This explains well under 1% of the variance (about 0.1% on eval). It is a weak description,
not a mechanism.

import math

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predicted activation at the newest token: a position-in-document curve."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0  # first token of a document (or of the row)
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    carry = (doc, pos)
    if pos == 0:
        return carry, -0.007
    # log-shaped drift: about +0.05 at position 1, 0 near position 31, floor -0.015
    return carry, max(-0.015, 0.07 - 0.015 * math.log2(pos + 1))
